newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil debt growth due to rollover of interest.
newsitem.headline: Brazil debt growth due to rollover of interest.

text.p: Brazil's internal debt is growing largely because of the capitalization of interest payments and not because of new issues, said Altamir Lopes, head of the Central Bank's economics department.

But Lopes said the growth was small, with net government securities, excluding debt-swap operations with the states, rising to an estimated 130.537 billion reais in August from 127.127 billion reais in July.
He said the Central Bank was "not concerned".
"Debt is rising because of the rollover of interest. But the rise is small," he told reporters.
Total net public sector debt in July was 249.158 billion reais, equivalent to 34.7 percent of gross domestic product, up from 243.632 billion reais or 34.3 percent of GDP in June.
Net internal debt stood at 217.644 billion reais in July, or 30.3 percent of GDP, up from 212.851 billion reais or 30 percent of GDP in June.

Lopes pointed out that real public sector debt-servicing costs had declined in GDP terms since the beginning of the year, falling to the equivalent of 3.51 percent of GDP by end-July compared with 4.2 percent of GDP in January.

Lopes acknowledged that real interest payments would rise in August and September because of lower-than-expected inflation. But he said he expected the gradual decline in real interest rates to continue after that.
